facts.text: East New Market earned its name when a 1776 land patent granted James Sulivane the title 'New Market,' just before the Declaration of Independence.
Settled in the 1600s, East New Market grew into a bustling trading post where Native Americans and European settlers exchanged goods.
A Greek‑revival Trinity Church, built around 1848, replaced the older Union Chapel and reflects the town’s 19th‑century religious architecture.
East New Market sits about six miles northeast of Cambridge, the Dorchester County seat, placing it within easy reach of four county capitals.
Many 17th‑century buildings survive in East New Market because economic hardship during the Great Depression halted new construction.
The town’s official site highlights East New Market’s rich history, celebrating its character and community pride through interactive maps and events.
